results.title: Sprout Social Layoffs 2026: 260 Employees Affected
results.content:
## Impact on Operations

The 260 affected employees span multiple departments, with the heaviest cuts falling in areas where AI automation now handles core functions. Sales support, customer success, and certain marketing operations roles saw significant reductions. Engineering teams focused on legacy infrastructure were also affected as the company consolidates resources around its next-generation AI product suite.

Sprout Social's primary operations are based in Chicago, Illinois, with additional teams working remotely across North America and in international markets. The layoffs affect employees across these locations. Affected workers received notification on July 15, 2026, and the company indicated it would provide severance packages and career transition support. [...] Sprout Social's July 2026 layoffs are part of a broader wave of AI-driven restructurings sweeping the SaaS and social media software sector, as companies race to embed generative AI into their core products while reducing headcount in functions being automated away. Competitors and peers in the social media management space have similarly realigned their workforces to reflect leaner, AI-augmented operating models. The broader tech industry has seen tens of thousands of layoffs in 2025 and 2026 as companies prioritize margin expansion and AI investment over headcount growth. For Sprout Social, the 20% workforce reduction signals a decisive pivot toward an AI-first product strategy intended to sustain long-term competitiveness against both legacy players and emerging AI-native entrants. [...] Sprout Social announced on July 15, 2026, that it is laying off 260 employees, representing 20% of its total workforce. The enterprise social media management company joins a growing list of tech firms restructuring operations as artificial intelligence reshapes the industry. The cuts signal a significant strategic pivot for the Chicago-based company, which has faced mounting pressure to reduce costs and accelerate its AI-driven product roadmap. The layoffs reflect broader tech industry trends that have seen companies aggressively trim headcount to fund automation investments and satisfy investor demands for profitability.

Sprout Social is laying off about 20% of its workforce, affecting roughly 260 employees, as the social media management company restructures its business amid rapid changes across the software industry.

The company began notifying affected employees on Wednesday. Chief Executive Ryan Barretto said the decision reflects broader shifts in how software companies are operating as artificial intelligence reshapes business priorities and investment strategies. [...] “Our industry, and software more broadly, is changing quickly,” he said. “The way companies need to operate and invest has changed with it.”

READ: Meta layoff forces H-1B worker to leave US (July 14, 2026)

The layoffs follow Sprout’s recent push into AI. In May, the company introduced an AI-powered social intelligence platform aimed at helping businesses better manage their social media presence. It also expanded Trellis, its agentic AI engine, with new capabilities for publishing content and analyzing social media data. [...] Sprout expects the restructuring to result in pre-tax charges of between $18 million and $20 million, largely related to severance and employee benefits. The company said most of those costs will be recorded during the third quarter, when the layoffs are expected to be completed.

Employees affected by the cuts will receive 12 weeks of base pay, plus an additional week of salary for each year of service. The company will also provide six months of fully paid healthcare coverage, a cash payment equal to the value of equity scheduled to vest over the next 90 days, and three months of outplacement assistance.
